title.value: Using Representation Expressiveness and Learnability to Evaluate Self-Supervised Learning Methods
title.justification: The title of the paper is explicitly stated in the provided reference information.
title.quote: Using Representation Expressiveness and Learnability to Evaluate Self-Supervised Learning Methods

extractions.description: The paper presents an evaluation framework for self-supervised learning (SSL) models by assessing the expressiveness and learnability of their representations. It introduces the Intrinsic Dimension (ID) for assessing expressiveness and Cluster Learnability (CL) for evaluating learnability. These metrics are combined into a single predictor called CLID, which is shown to correlate with model performance on various visual classification tasks.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is primarily focused on proposing an evaluation framework for self-supervised learning models, which is more aligned with machine learning and artificial intelligence than with climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We address the problem of evaluating the quality of self-supervised learning (SSL) models without access to supervised labels, while being agnostic to the architecture, learning algorithm or data manipulation used during training.

primary_category.justification: The central theme of the paper revolves around evaluating SSL models using new metrics. It focuses on machine learning methodologies rather than direct climate or ecological sustainable development applications.
primary_category.quote: We propose an evaluation framework for self-supervised learning relying on expressiveness and learnability, yielding new insights into existing techniques in the literature.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address any specific secondary themes related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: Our contributions are summarized below: • We propose an evaluation framework for self-supervised learning relying on expressiveness and learnability, yielding new insights into existing techniques in the literature.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any specific sub-categories under climate or ecological sustainable development, as it mainly advances self-supervised learning evaluation techniques.
primary_sub_category.quote: To assess learnability, we take inspiration from Laina et al. (2020) and propose a novel method called Cluster Learnability (CL), based on the performance of a KNN learner trained to predict labels induced by clustering held-out representations with K-Means.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Similarly, there are no secondary sub-categories related to climate or ecological issues discussed in the paper.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We propose to quantify expressiveness via an estimator of the intrinsic dimension (ID) of the data representations.

applications.value: Evaluation framework for self-supervised learning (SSL) models
applications.justification: The paper introduces a new framework (CLID) to evaluate self-supervised learning models based on expressiveness and learnability, which could be applicable for comparing and selecting SSL models across various classification tasks.
applications.quote: We propose to quantify expressiveness via an estimator of the intrinsic dimension (ID) of the data representations (Facco et al., 2017; Ansuini et al., 2019). To assess learnability, we take inspiration from Laina et al. (2020) and propose a novel method called Cluster Learnability (CL).
